specification.problem: Pattern classification by a Trugenberger-style quantum Hamming-distance computation: load N binarized training patterns with class labels in superposition, imprint the Hamming distance to a query as a relative phase on an ancilla, interfere, post-select a=0, and read the class by a cos^2-weighted vote.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance (assumed): n=2 pattern bits, m=1 label bit, N=4 training patterns with 2 per class, one ancilla, loaded by standard gates (X plus multi-controlled X on a basis-state index scheme, or via an index register). The query is classical and loaded by X gates, so the x register can be dropped. Outside scope: the paper's exact MNIST preprocessing, the exact loading procedure, resource analysis, and any claimed advantage over classical classifiers. The exact paper algorithm is not reproduced, only the Trugenberger-based family.

symbols.meaning: number of pattern bits (binarized downscaled pixels)
Hamming distance between p_k and x

equations.label: Training superposition
equations.description: Uniform-weight superposition of patterns entangled with labels, ancilla in |0>.
equations.justification: Standard Trugenberger memory state; the abstract only names his Hamming-distance proposal. Uniform weights are assumed.
assumptions: loaded with standard gates, not initialize

equations.label: Query XOR encoding
equations.latex: |p_k\rangle\to|p_k\oplus x\rangle=|d_k^{(1)}\ldots d_k^{(n)}\rangle,\quad d_k^{(j)}=p_{k,j}\oplus x_j,\quad d_k=\sum_j d_k^{(j)}
equations.description: Apply X on p qubits where x_j=1 (classical query). The qubit j is 1 where the pattern disagrees with the query, so the Hamming weight is d_k. The sketch's extra X for XNOR would give n-d_k instead, so omit it.
equations.justification: Hamming distance equals weight of the XOR. This is a choice of encoding.
assumptions: no extra X layer, otherwise d is replaced by n-d

equations.label: Distance phase on ancilla
equations.latex: H_a;\ \prod_{j}\mathrm{CP}_{a\to p_j}(-\pi/n)\text{ with }a\text{ in }|1\rangle\text{ branch};\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(|0\rangle+e^{-i\pi d_k/n}|1\rangle\right)
equations.description: After H on a, a controlled phase of angle -pi/n on each pattern qubit (control a) gives the 1 branch the phase exp(-i pi d_k/n). To get the sketch's half angle exp(-i pi d/(2n)) relative phase symmetrically, use angle pi/(2n) per qubit with Z/phase compensation on a, or use a phase of pi/(2n) per qubit directly (the P gate then has angle -pi/(2n)).
equations.justification: Recalled from Trugenberger's phase-estimation-free Hamming distance scheme. The angle convention is fixed here so that the final probability matches eq_4.
assumptions: use per-qubit angle theta=-pi/(2n)*... chosen so total relative phase is -pi d_k/(2n)*2 or -pi d_k/(2n) consistently with eq_4

equations.label: Ancilla outcome probability
equations.description: After the final H on a, interference gives P(a=0) for pattern k. This requires relative phase exp(-i pi d_k/n) between the branches, i.e. P=(1+cos(phi))/2 with phi=pi d_k/n.
equations.abstract_quote: draws on Trugenberger’s proposal for measuring the Hamming distance on a quantum computer
equations.justification: Inferred from the Trugenberger scheme and the sketch. The relative phase pi d/n gives cos^2(pi d/(2n)), so the per-qubit phase must be pi/n, not pi/(2n).

equations.label: Class posterior and decision
equations.latex: P(c\mid a=0)=\frac{\sum_{k:c_k=c}\cos^2(\pi d_k/2n)}{\sum_{k}\cos^2(\pi d_k/2n)},\quad \hat c=\arg\max_c P(c\mid a=0)
equations.description: Classification by the post-selected distribution over the class register.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_1 and eq_4 with uniform weights; the paper's exact decision rule is not known.

registers.name: p
registers.role: pattern register, becomes the XOR/difference register

registers.name: loader ancillas
registers.role: index register or work qubits for state preparation, to be uncomputed

steps.description: Load training superposition of (pattern,label) pairs with standard gates (for example a small index register with H, then multi-controlled X to write p_k and c_k, then uncompute the index if feasible; otherwise keep the index as an extra register and do not measure it).
Apply X on p_j for each j where x_j=1, so p holds the difference bits.
Apply H on a, then controlled-phase gates from a onto each p_j with angle -pi/n.
Apply H on a, measure a and c (and nothing else).
Postprocess: keep shots with a=0, tally c, take argmax.

specification.measurement: Measure a and c only. Qiskit little-endian: if classical bits are ordered [c0..c_{m-1}, a], the counts key string reversed gives bit i at index i.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Filter counts with a=0, marginalize onto c bits (reverse the key string to index by bit), take the argmax label; ties broken arbitrarily. Optionally compare with the exact cos^2-weighted vote computed classically.
assumptions: Tiny instance n=2, m=1, N=4 chosen by me; the real task may differ
No oracle or black box is used; the query is loaded by X gates
missing_information: The paper's exact phase/angle convention and decision rule
Whether the paper uses a different measurement or amplification scheme
